taxonomic_note: Accepted project concept. Hays and Travis are locked; a historical Berlandier specimen spanning the Bejar-to-Austin corridor is too geographically ambiguous to assign to a third county.
look_here_first: Start with the narrow opposite leaves and upright terminal spike of pink-lavender bilabiate flowers. Compare leaf width and habitat carefully against P. correllii and the broad P. virginiana complex.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays is supported by preserved BRIT/SMU specimen BRIT367184 south of Dripping Springs; Travis is supported by UT Plant Resources Center. The historical Bejar-to-Austin specimen is intentionally not assigned to a county.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the two-county HOLD.

best_field_traits: terminal spike of pink to lavender bilabiate flowers
flowers arranged in repeated clusters along the spike
narrow foliage is an important first-pass cue
morphology_keys.comparison_training: P. correllii is a tall rhizomatous wetland/stream-edge specialist; the P. virginiana complex is broader and taxonomically messy in Texas. For P. angustifolia, begin with the notably narrow leaves and then confirm floral/spike characters.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use narrow foliage plus the Physostegia spike architecture; do not identify from pink flowers alone.
